title: Pattern Headings: Wars
scope: Free-floating subdivisions used under headings for individual wars (including coups, revolutions, insurrections, uprisings, invasions, civil wars), entered directly under their names or as subdivisions under place names; not battles, riots, unarmed disturbances, terrorist attacks, or metaphorical 'wars'.
general_notes: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

Subdivisions on this list with the notation (May Subd Geog) should be further subdivided by place only when used after a war established directly under its name, for example, World War, 1939-1945. For a war that is established under its own name and that was fought in a single jurisdiction that is either incorporated or implied in the name, further subdivide by place in accordance with H 830 only to bring out a place other than the one named or implied in the heading, or to bring out a locality within that place. For a war established as a subdivision under the name of a place, the subdivisions on this list should not be further subdivided by place. (sec. F.1)
Entry notes citing 'sec. E.2 and sec. E.3.a' refer to the --Participation provisions now at sec. F.2 and sec. F.3.a.

[LC practice] In early 2025, the use of form subdivisions was phased out. Library of Congress catalogers assign Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. Therefore, the form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by Library of Congress catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.
